saints.name: Dionysius of Paris
saints.dates: Third century; martyrdom in 258 in the OCA account

summary.text: A bishop and martyr associated with the early Christian mission in Paris. The OCA explicitly distinguishes him from Saint Dionysius the Areopagite of Athens.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: Known also as Denis or Denys, he is remembered as a patron of France. His birthplace and early life are not detailed in this OCA entry.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The received account places his mission to Lutetia, modern Paris, around 250. It connects his remembrance with Montmartre and the later abbey of Saint-Denis.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The OCA dates his beheading with two fellow Christians to 258. It explicitly labels the story of carrying his severed head as a later legend.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: A medieval identification with the Areopagite should not erase the distinction between these saints. The OCA gives Dionysius of Paris an October 9 commemoration; the Areopagite is commemorated on October 3.
